blocks.text: Ezekiel 48 closes the vision in chapters 40–48, which ranges across a measured sanctuary, returning glory, altar, priests and Levites, the prince, offerings, land, river, tribes, resident aliens, and the city named “Jehovah is there.” This chapter gathers several of those concerns into its ordered distribution of land, central sacred area, city, and tribal gates. Questions about how the book reached its received form remain debated: it sustains an Ezekielian first-person voice while also showing collection, coordination, repetition, and textual development compatible with scribal shaping. A five-part outline—chapters 1–3, 4–24, 25–32, 33–39, and 40–48—can help orient a reader without deciding questions of chronology or composition.
